recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to Ingredient/SubstanceDefinition guidance should be handled by a new BRR decision rather than by restoring the superseded FHIR-31822 warning.
issue_request: FHIR-31822 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and requested a Here Be Dragons warning on SubstanceDefinition plus guidance that users understand the difference between Ingredient and SubstanceDefinition because SubstanceDefinition might change significantly while its 80 percent fit was reviewed.
initial_application: Git commit 59ffd1065202cf6338c52ccb557c07637464edea applied FHIR-31822 by expanding source/substancedefinition/substancedefinition-introduction.xml with scope text, Ingredient/Substance/Medication boundary guidance, and the then-approved dragon warning.
additional_context: Ingredient and SubstanceDefinition are active BRR resources in source/fhir.ini. Current SubstanceDefinition text preserves the definitional-versus-ingredient distinction; current Ingredient text and definitions describe Ingredient as product-context material with role and strength and permit SubstanceDefinition references where detailed substance definition is needed. Later issues FHIR-31841, FHIR-39138, and FHIR-48405 refined or audited the same area, and FHIR-50941 later approved removing the dragon warning because SubstanceDefinition had stabilized.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Restoring the dragon warning would contradict FHIR-50941, and adding another Ingredient note would duplicate current build-scope guidance.
